subject: Texas AI Docket, Carousel No. 9, August 22nd, 2026, The rule that never says data center
body:

Carousel No. 9, August 22nd, 2026

Did NOT meet the bar: 6.56 against 7.0. Read before posting.

This run did not merge, so the images below come from the run branch claude/daily-2026-08-22 rather than from main. They stop resolving if that branch is deleted.

What degraded

  • NO ITEM WAS ADMITTED TO THE RECORD. Seven items pass every gate and the admission bar and are held in seed/docket_seed.json instead. Admitting them turns site_build.py red, and this run MEASURED that rather than arguing it: a merged 76 item ledger was built into a scratch directory and the build exited 1 on construction/index.html: 44, while the same build at 69 items exits 0. The defect sits in scripts/site/site_build.py, which ownership.yaml puts in the human lane, so no automation here may fix it. The run record carries the diagnosis, the measurement and the proposed fix at the top.
  • The seven held items were ALSO failing the promote gate on a missing movement line, which was this run's own defect and is now fixed. The first draft of the run record claimed they passed every gate and they did not. Seven movement lines were written into the seed and the gate now admits all seven, which is what made the measurement above possible.
  • The scanner's daily ceiling was NOT checked. The Supabase connector is not available in this session, so the scanner.scans query could not be run.
  • The water map's pin count could not be checked the way the routine describes. The map's circles are tank and rim pairs rather than one circle per reservoir, so the count is not comparable to the reservoir figure. Recorded as NOT SETTLED rather than as fine.
  • Phase 1's craft refresh ran as two searches rather than the usual ten, on the rotating focus of threshold and numeral typography.
  • THE DECK DID NOT MEET THE BAR AND DID NOT MERGE. Six panels, medians 6.77, 7.40, 6.98, 6.87 and 6.56 against a floor of 7.0. Panel one hard-failed a count over an index the deck reads 10 of 34 rows from, and that defect class turned up twice more, so the repair was applied as a rule. Panel six hard-failed the RECORD rather than the deck, and that finding is the most important thing this run produced. Every lens asked for one plain sentence saying what the rule would do to a Texan, and a judge supplied the answer this run should have taken: the statute quote already fetched and sitting in tx-2026-0002-c10 carries it, so quoting it is not inferring. That is the next run's first move.
  • THE RECORD PUBLISHED FOUR ASSERTIONS THIS RUN'S OWN FACT-CHECKER REFUSED, and the first correction missed the field that mattered most. tx-2026-0002 said the rule is the category that covers data centers and that individual Texans had filed, and quoted 33 filings while stamped verified today on a page fetched at 34. The summary was fixed and public_access.how was not, which is what the site publishes as How to take part, and the history line written with that fix claimed it had been done. Both are corrected and a second history line says what the first one missed.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it The rule that never says data center, paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

1. The post copy

September 4th shuts the comment window.

Until then it is open on 16 TAC Section 25.521, the Large Load Demand Management Service rule proposed by the Public Utility Commission of Texas. It would have ERCOT competitively procure demand reductions from large load customers.

The rule as published in the Texas Register never writes the words data center. It draws a line instead. A large load customer is an entity with total non-coincident peak demand at a single site of 75 megawatts or more.

Comments run through the interchange on the commission's website at interchange.puc.texas.gov. Each should refer to Project Number 58482.

The index stands at 34 filings. The Data Center Coalition is in it. So is CyrusOne, LP. So is item 33, under the party name Helen Bryant with item type PC.

That is all the index carries. An item number. A file stamp. A party name. An item type. A filing description. Nothing on that page says who Helen Bryant is.

#Project58482 #LargeLoadDemandManagement #PUCT
